To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

pre- service teachers' discourses on becoming a physical education teacher are characterized by the following elements: (i) the teacher's mission is a central issue in the construction of their professional identity; (ii) their learning to teach is a process of becoming a teacher, which is a social and collective construction; and (iii) they construct their professional identity in relation to others.

the pre-service teachers' discourses about themselves and others, as well as the images they produced, portrayed the physical education teacher in a positive light and as a professional who is concerned about the quality of the teaching practice and about their professional development, in the context of a dialogic relation with others.

the pre-service teachers in this study (re)constructed their professional identity in a dialogical relationship between talk and images in which they: (i) portrayed themselves in the role of a physical education teacher; (ii) recognized the importance of their learning-to-teach experiences and the social recognition of others; and (iii) acknowledged the importance of their mission as teachers.
